To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) there are good moral reasons for using animals in preclinical safety research for ARTs, (2) there are good reasons not to use animals in preclinical efficacy research for ARTs.

(1) the use of animal research for testing ARTs is morally justified, (2) this is because the benefits of the use of animal-based research for testing ART outweigh the harm done to the animals involved, (3) this is because, in the absence of animal research for safety testing, the use of new ARTs in humans is likely to result in serious harm and (4) this is because animal research is necessary for testing the safety of ARTs.

(1) the moral importance of safety research for new ARTs outweighs the limited infringements of the wellbeing of animals, (2) animal welfare should be maximized in the design of the experiments and (3) the use of animals is ethically justified only when the results of the animal experiments are relevant for human patients
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ethics of animal research for the preclinical development of new ARTs.
the ethics of preclinical research with animals for the development of new ARTs and the use of animals in preclinical safety research for ARTs.
the ethics of the use of animal research models for preclinical research on ARTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, on balance, animal welfare is better served by allowing animal research for ARTs than by banning it.
animal welfare should not be the sole or even the main criterion for evaluating ART research.

the use of preclinical animal testing is ethically acceptable for the development and testing of new ART, but only if the research meets a number of conditions, which include a thorough justification for the use of animals and the application of the three R's.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of animal for pre-clinical testing of ARTs can be morally justified, but only under certain conditions.
we have provided an argument in favour of the use of non-human animals in the field of preclinical research for ART, and we have shown that this use can be morally justified.

the use of animal research in ART research is justified when it meets three requirements: (1) the use of animals is necessary, (2) the animal research contributes to a specific goal, (3) the use of animal is proportional to the goal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of animal research for ART research is ethically justifiable.
the use of animal research in the development and pre-clinical testing of new ART is not only morally permissible, but also morally required.
animal research is justified insofar as it is a necessary step towards the development of new ARTs that are safe and effective for humans.
